summary: @servicetitan/link-item ships obfuscated preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute a 727 KB opaque bundle
details: The package is advertised as a small React link-item component (three tiny.tsx files under src/, a ~104-byte dist/index.js main). The tarball additionally ships an obfuscated preinstall script (setup.mjs) and a 727 KB single-line obfuscated payload (math_init.js, marked `// @bun @bun-cjs`, using a shuffled string-array rotator and a decoder function). package.json declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`, so on `npm install` setup.mjs runs automatically; it downloads a Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/....zip`, extracts and chmod +x's the Bun binary in a temp directory, then invokes it with `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')],...)` to execute the sibling bundle. Fetching an alternate JavaScript runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated bundle at install time bypasses Node.js resolution and static inspection and is unrelated to the package's advertised purpose. The obfuscated payload's behavior cannot be characterized from source, but the delivery shape (obfuscated preinstall + fetched alternate runtime + opaque 727 KB payload auto-executed) is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern. The mismatch between the declared @servicetitan/link-item scope+repo (servicetitan/anvil-uikit-contrib) and the shipped dropper/bundle is consistent with a scope or maintainer-account compromise.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
